5. It is further stated that when the present plaintiff-opposite party was an absolute owner and possessor went to the relevant authority on 13-12-2004 to pay the annual rent (খাজনা) but she came to know that during the last Revenue Survey the suit property has been mutated in the name of the present defendant-petitioners government and she was denied to pay rent (খাজনা) for the suit land. After being confirmed about the recording of the Revenue Survey (SA) in the name of government, the present plaintiff-opposite party filed the present suit for declaring the recording in RS Khatian in the name of Government as illegally and unlawfully made by the office of the government by a gross mistake and not binding upon the present-opposite party. 

 6. The present defendant-petitioner, the government appeared and contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint and contending that the suit land was correctly recorded in the name of the government and since the land is recorded in favour of the Bangladesh Government all title and interest have been vested upon the government. 

 10. He further submits that in the present proceeding of the suit the learned trial court passed the order No. 14 dated 21-5-2005 appointing an Advocate Commissioner to submit a report after obtaining statement of the concerned lawyer and accordingly on 1-6-2005 the learned Advocate Commissioner submitted its report but he was not called in as a witness thus the defendant-petitioners did not have any opportunity to cross-examine as to the report which is illegal and unacceptable thus the finding of the Lower Appellate Court by the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. In support of his above contention he referred to a case of Abdul Noor (Md) alias Gunnu Mia and another vs. Makhan Mia alias Md Laisuzzaman reported in 60 DLR (AD) at page 39 which reads as follows:- 

 "The presumption of correctness as to CS record of right is not certainly available with regard to this State Acquisition Khatians. There is no presumption of correctness in respect of the State Acquisition Khatians as it is to be found in case of CS Khatians in pursuance of the provision under section 103-B of the Bengal Tenancy Act". 

 AND WHEREAS the lands of khatian No. 16 of Mouza Dhanmondai was recorded in the name of one Dukhini Bewa who surrendered the same in favour of the land-lord, the Dacca Nowab Estate and the latter settled it out to Surya Kumar Bose who while owning and possessing the lands of Khatian No. 16 of Mouza Dhanmondai in raiyati jote right for more than 12 years sold the same to Wazuddin and Mahmuda Begum by registered sale deed dated 18-9-1952. 

 24. He further submits that if there is conflict between the records of right i.e. SA, RS and BS then the latest record of right should prevail over any other record. In support of his contention he submitted a case of Fatema Khatun vs Fazil Mia reported in 21 BLD 14 = 6 BLC which reads as follows: State acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (XXVIII of 1951) section-144A. 

 27. After considering the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the parties and also perusing the application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure along with the annexures, judgment and decree, particularly the impugned judgment passed on 30-11-2005, it appears to me that the suit land appertaining to CS Khatian No. 168 and 16 and CS Dag Nos. 724, 733 and 734 corresponding to SA Dag Nos. 882 and 883 measuring total land of 0.15 acres of land was originally owned and possessed by one Ahsan Ullah Bhuiyan through a long transfer of rayati tenancy as mentioned in the documents executed in favour of Meherunnessa Chowdhury, the mother of the present plaintiff-opposite party. The said Meherunnessa Chowdhury while was an absolute owner and possessor of the suit land mutated her name after complying all required formalities for recording the suit land in her name and paying rent (খাজনা) to the Government. She transferred the suit land to her daughter by 2(two) registered deeds of heba-bil-ewaz being Nos. 4431 and 4432 both dated 14-4-1997. The present opposite party after becoming the possessor of the suit land mutated her name with the relevant Government Authority and duly paid rent (খাজনা) with the said authority having acquired record of right in the State Acquisition (SA) Survey in favour of the predecessor of the opposite party on the basis of the above record of right her name was mutated pursuant to the Mutation Case No. 515-P-1 of 77-78 and 516-P-1 of 77-78 and enjoying the possession therefrom. 

 30. Regarding the submission made by the learned advocate for the petitioners as to the change of title which needed to be proved by plaintiff-opposite party in the trial court. In such matter I consider that in the instant case the deeds or transductions from 1962 until 1997 have not been challenged by the Government or title deeds have not been invalidated, thus, the documents exhibited being exhibit Nos. 5, 7 and 7 (a) remained valid documents for the ownership of the suit land and without contradicting the validity of such documents a chain of title cannot be broken and thereby record of right in Revision Survey (RS) in favour of the Government cannot take way the title and right of the plaintiff opposite party from the suit land. It is well established principle that valid deeds are the principal documents for the ownership of a land and record of right under the Tenancy Rules , 1953 are to be considered as supporting documents and possession therefrom for creating entitlement on a land. So, the chain has not been broken to introduce any new record of right.
